title: Graph-in-Graph Network for Automatic Gene Ontology Description Generation

problem.claim: Gene Ontology terms represent gene functions, and descriptions need to be generated for terms in the molecular function, biological process, and cellular component categories.

gap.claim: Existing research mainly predicts gene-term associations, while generating descriptions for new terms is rarely pursued.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes automatic GO term description generation.
The paper proposes a Graph-in-Graph network that uses a graph of GO terms whose nodes are gene graphs to leverage GO structural information.
The authors build three large-scale benchmark datasets to validate the proposed network.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe GO term description generation as a novel task.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the Graph-in-Graph network can derive biological functions of GO terms and generate proper descriptions.

The authors report substantial performance improvements for seven sequence-to-sequence models across all evaluation metrics, with up to 34.7% relative improvement in BLEU, 14.5% in ROUGE-L, and 39.1% in METEOR.

narrative_sequence.summary: GO is a primary gene function knowledge base, and its basic element is a term grouping genes with the same function.
Prior work mainly predicts gene-term associations, whereas description generation for new terms is rarely pursued.
The paper introduces GO term description generation for three GO categories.
It proposes a two-layer Graph-in-Graph network that represents GO terms as nodes containing gene graphs and leverages GO structure.
Three benchmark datasets are built, and improvements are reported across seven sequence-to-sequence models and all evaluation metrics.
